claim: TubeArchivist advises a ~3s sleep interval between YouTube requests to avoid throttling, a 90-day refresh window to spread requests, and notes residential IPs can get throttled (a shared proxy/VPN IP may help).
quote: Sleep Interval: Time in seconds to sleep between requests to YouTube. It's a good idea to set this to 3 seconds... some users have reported throttling issues from residential IP address ranges. You might be able to avoid that with a shared IP from a Proxy/VPN.
verify_note: paraphrased composite from TubeArchivist Settings/FAQ docs

claim: TubeSync tells users to keep index frequency as long as possible (up to 24h) and warns that crawling large amounts quickly can get your IP throttled or banned by the source.
quote: It's a good idea to add sources with as long of an index frequency as possible... Try and keep this as long as possible, up to 24 hours... It's entirely possible that your IP address could get throttled and/or banned, by the source, if you try to crawl extremely large amounts quickly. Try to be polite with the smallest amount of indexing and concurrent downloads possible.

claim: PinchFlat self-throttles via a configurable worker concurrency (YT_DLP_WORKER_CONCURRENCY), recommends setting it to 1 if IP-limited, because being too aggressive causes Google to rate-limit the IP and fail indexing/downloads.
quote: Pinchflat is configured to only perform a certain number of operations at the same time because being too aggressive in fetching/downloading content will result in Google rate limiting your IP... set this to 1 if you're getting IP limited.

claim: In Feb 2026 (yt-dlp stable 2026.02.04) a wave hit where all public, login-free YouTube videos began returning LOGIN_REQUIRED 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot', with the error itself suggesting cookies, updating to nightly/master, and PO tokens.
quote: Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. Use --cookies-from-browser or --cookies for the authentication... LOGIN_REQUIRED status [across web, web_safari, android_vr]
verify_note: issue title: All public YouTube videos require login

claim: PO Tokens (proof-of-origin) are generated by BotGuard/DroidGuard/iOSGuard, are bound to the video/session and expire fast, and YouTube continuously updates enforcement so the guidance is provisional.
quote: PO Tokens are still an active area of research, and YouTube is continuously updating the implementation and enforcement... A PO Token is generated by either BotGuard (Web), DroidGuard (Android), or iOSGuard (iOS), and a PO Token from one platform cannot be used on another.

claim: The bgutil POT provider runs alongside yt-dlp (preferably as an always-running HTTP server with a prebuilt Docker image) to generate PO tokens on demand, which yt-dlp picks up automatically; HTTP-server mode is recommended for production with repeated requests.
quote: What works is a small helper called bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider running on the side; it generates tokens on demand and the main yt-dlp call picks them up automatically... HTTP server mode is recommended for production deployments with multiple requests.

claim: Providing a PO token does not guarantee bypassing 403/bot checks but makes traffic appear more legitimate; install via pip as a yt-dlp plugin.
quote: Providing a PO token does not guarantee bypassing 403 errors or bot checks, but it may help your traffic seem more legitimate.

claim: yt-dlp's cookie-export guidance exists precisely because YouTube rotates and invalidates cookies on continued browser use: export from a fresh private/incognito window, then close it so the session is never reopened, otherwise the cookies are invalidated.
quote: Open a new private browsing/incognito window and log into YouTube... Export youtube.com cookies from the browser... Close the private browsing/incognito window so that the session is never opened in the browser again.

claim: Users report that authenticating yt-dlp with browser cookies carries account ban risk (temporary or permanent), motivating throwaway accounts and caution on request rate/volume.
quote: Question about risk of using cookies-from-browser... whether YouTube permanently bans accounts for using cookies with yt-dlp [and] whether cookies remain valid when used outside the browser
verify_note: issue is a user question; ban-risk framing also in yt-dlp docs
